papers.title_in_file: Unleashed from Constrained Optimization: Quantum Computing for Quantum Chemistry Employing Generator Coordinate Inspired Method
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method, numerical and hardware experiments, discussion
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation paper, with one small IBM hardware test, on a generator-coordinate-inspired subspace method added to ADAPT-VQE for quantum chemistry.

assertions.value: The authors report that for a strongly correlated stretched H6 molecule the GCIM approaches completed in 12∼13 seconds, while ADAPT-VQE required approximately four hours to achieve a similar level of accuracy.
assertions.anchor: Numerical and Real Hardware Experiments, p.8
quotes: For example, for the strongly correlated H6 molecule at a stretched H
the GCIM approaches completed in 12∼13 seconds, while ADAPT-VQE required approximately four hours to achieve a similar level of accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they ran numerical experiments on four molecular systems across seven geometries, and that all experiments use the STO-3G basis.
assertions.anchor: Numerical and Real Hardware Experiments, p.6
quotes: We have performed numerical experiments on four molecular systems across seven geometries
All experiments use STO-3G basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Numerical and Real Hardware Experiments, p.6.

assertions.value: The authors state that the non-orthogonality of the generating functions necessitates extra resources for evaluating the off-diagonal matrix elements and the entire overlap matrix.
quotes: This non-orthogonality necessitates extra resources for evaluating the associated off-diagonal matrix elements and the entire overlap matrix for solving a generalized eigenvalue problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its method, p.4.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Quantum Computers: Towards a Standard Performance Evaluation Approach
papers.what_it_is: A review and position paper on quantum computer benchmarking that proposes guidelines and quality attributes for benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quality attributes of a good benchmark are relevance, reproducibility, fairness, verifiability and usability.
quotes: we can still leverage some of the lessons learned such as the quality attributes of a good benchmark such as relevance, reproducibility, fairness, verifiability and usability.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' proposal, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose general guidelines for quantum benchmarking, aimed at a roadmap towards standardizing the performance evaluation of quantum devices.
quotes: we propose general guidelines for quantum benchmarking. These guidelines aim to pave the way for establishing a roadmap towards standardizing the performance evaluation of quantum devices
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that meeting all of the quality attributes simultaneously can be challenging.
quotes: It is important to note that meeting all these attributes simultaneously can be challenging.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit, Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: The Hintons in your Neural Network: a Quantum Field Theory View of Deep Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and contributions, conclusion and outlook
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical paper that formulates deep learning as a quantum field theory on Gaussian states, mappable to optical quantum computers.

assertions.value: The authors state that their contribution is theoretical and that they do not expect their tractable approximations to perform better than their classical cousins.
quotes: we emphasize that our contribution is theoretical; we do not expect that these tractable approximations perform better than their classical cousins.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope, Introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that input signals are encoded in Gaussian states and that linear and non-linear layers can be represented as unitary quantum gates.
quotes: input signals are encoded in Gaussian states, a generalization of Gaussian processes
We show how to represent linear and non-linear layers as unitary quantum gates
assertions.certainty_reason: Theoretical construction stated in the abstract; no proof is cited here.

assertions.value: The authors state that they chose not to benchmark the tractable limits against classical models, because they do not expect them to perform better.
quotes: But because we do not expect that these tractable limits perform any better than classical models we choose not to benchmark them against each other.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit, Conclusion and Outlook.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Radio Astronomy: Data Encodings and Quantum Image Processing
papers.what_it_is: A study of quantum image encodings and a toy image reconstruction pipeline for radio interferometry, with a proposed variational self-calibration algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors state that for identifying and locating bright radio sources, quantum computing can offer an exponential speedup over classical algorithms, even when accounting for data encoding cost and repeated circuit evaluations.
quotes: For identifying and locating bright radio sources, quantum computing can offer an exponential speedup over classical algorithms, even when accounting for data encoding cost and repeated circuit evaluations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim from a toy pipeline, not a proof.

assertions.value: The authors report that of the different quantum image encodings, the QPIE encoding offers excellent algorithmic speedup without sacrificing image fidelity, and that the evaluation used a toy image reconstruction pipeline.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Conclusion, p.1 and p.9
quotes: We evaluate the suitability of different quantum image representations using a toy quantum computing image reconstruction pipeline
Of the different quantum image encodings, we find that the QPIE encoding offers excellent algorithmic speedup without sacrificing image fidelity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one toy study.

assertions.value: The authors state that measurement of the quantum state destroys the superposition, so multiple measurements require re-encoding and re-measuring the state, which can undermine quantum advantage.
quotes: measurement of the quantum state is a probabilistic result which destroys the superposition. To perform multiple measurements, one must re-encode and re-measure the state, which can undermine quantum advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit, Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: Machine-learning based noise characterization and correction on neutral atoms NISQ devices
papers.what_it_is: A study that trains machine learning models to characterize noise parameters, and a reinforcement learning agent to design correction pulses, on Pasqal neutral atom devices.

assertions.value: The authors report that ANN models performed better than linear regression in predicting the laser intensity fluctuation, and that model accuracy increases with both the number of qubits and the number of measurements.
quotes: We found that ANN perform better than linear regression and that the model accuracies increases both with the number of qubits and with the number of measurements.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, mostly on simulated data.

assertions.value: The authors state that the characterization models were trained on a dataset of simulated noisy measurements of Pasqal machines and tested on real data, and that the correction model was trained on a simulated test setting.
quotes: To characterize the noise we collected a dataset of multiple simulated noisy measurement of different settings in Pasqal quantum machines to train ML models and we test them on real data.
For the noise correction we trained a RL model to find a correction pulse to counteract the effects of the noise affecting a simulated test setting.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Conclusions and Outlooks.

assertions.value: The authors state that they have insights that characterizing the noise parameters is more effective by increasing the number of measurements than by increasing the number of qubits.
quotes: we have insights that in order to better characterize the noise parameters it is more effective to increase the number of measurements respect to the number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors call this an insight, from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Reservoir Computing via Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion section VII.A, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A quantum machine learning paper applying reservoir computing to quantum recurrent networks (QRNN, QLSTM, QGRU) for function approximation and time series prediction, by Wells Fargo and IBM authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that numerical simulations show QRNN-RC can reach results comparable to fully trained QRNN models in several function approximation and time-series prediction tasks.
quotes: We show via numerical simulations that the QRNN-RC can reach results comparable to fully trained QRNN models in several function approximation and time-series prediction tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that compared with classical RNN-based reservoir computing, the quantum solutions require fewer training epochs in most cases.
quotes: We also compare to classical RNN-based RC and show that the quantum solutions require fewer training epochs in most cases.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the reservoir computing approach the QRNN with randomly initialized weights is treated as a dynamical system and only the final classical linear layer is trained.
quotes: The main idea to this RC approach is that the QRNN with randomly initialized weights is treated as a dynamical system and only the final classical linear layer is trained.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Abstract.

papers.title_in_file: Training Computer Scientists for the Challenges of Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusion and future work

assertions.value: The authors state that the development creates a gap in current computer science curricula, since most quantum computing lectures are strongly physics-oriented and have little intersection with the remaining curriculum of computer science.
quotes: this development creates a gap in current computer science curricula since most quantum computing lectures are strongly physics-oriented and have little intersection with the remaining curriculum of computer science.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim without data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they designed a new lecture and exercise series on Hybrid Quantum-Classical Systems, where students learn how to decompose applications and implement computational tasks on a hybrid quantum-classical computational continuum.
quotes: we designed a new lecture and exercise series on Hybrid Quantum-Classical Systems, where students learn how to decompose applications and implement computational tasks on a hybrid quantum-classical computational continuum.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that surveys could provide insights into the reception of the course and evaluate its effectiveness, as a future refinement.
quotes: Regarding future refinements of the course, the implementation of surveys could provide insights into the reception of our course and evaluate its effectiveness and areas for improvement with regard to defined learning outcomes.

papers.title_in_file: Greedy Gradient-free Adaptive Variational Quantum Algorithms on a Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum Computer
papers.what_it_is: An algorithm paper introducing GGA-VQE, a greedy gradient-free adaptive VQE, tested on emulators and on a 25-qubit QPU.

assertions.value: The authors state that on an HPC emulator with statistical noise, for the H2O and LiH molecules, the local optimisation step is more resilient to measurement noise than a global optimisation procedure, and that GGA-VQE thus outperforms ADAPT-VQE.
quotes: we have computed the ground states of the H2O and LiH molecules on an HPC emulator in the presence of statistical noise arising from the finite number of observable evaluations.
In both cases we show that the local optimisation step is more resilient to measurement noise than a global optimisation procedure and GGA-VQE thus outperforms ADAPT-VQE.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from emulator runs in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that on real quantum hardware GGA-VQE computed the ground state of an open boundary 25-qubit transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian, with a ground state fidelity of over 98%, evaluated by noiseless emulation of the circuit retrieved from the QPU.
assertions.anchor: Discussion and Abstract, p.1 and p.9
quotes: we have used the GGA-VQE algorithm to successfully compute the ground state of an open boundary 25-qubit transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian, achieving a ground state fidelity of over 98%.
We demonstrate this by retrieving the parameterized operators calculated on the QPU and evaluating the resulting ansatz wave-function via noiseless emulation
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors state that for a strongly correlated stretched linear H6 chain both ADAPT-VQE and GGA-VQE perform poorly, and that hardware noise on the QPU produces inaccurate energies.
assertions.anchor: Discussion and Abstract, p.1 and p.9
quotes: we have applied the GGA-VQE algorithm to compute the ground state of a strongly correlated stretched linear H6 chain.
While both the ADAPT-VQE algorithm and the GGA-VQE algorithm perform poorly for this challenging system
Although hardware noise on the QPU produces inaccurate energies
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of limits, Abstract and Discussion.
